source_text:
Κατὰ κυριακὴν δὲ κυρίου συναχθέντες κλάσατε ἄρτον καὶ εὐχαριστήσατε, προεξομολογησάμενοι τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν, ὅπως καθαρὰ ἡ θυσία ὑμῶν ᾖ.
πᾶς δὲ ἔχων τὴν ἀμφιβολίαν μετὰ τοῦ ἑταίρου αὐτοῦ μὴ συνελθέτω ὑμῖν, ἕως ὁ??ʼ διαλλαγῶσιν, ἵνα μὴ κοινωθῇ ἡ θυσία ὑμῶν.
αὕτη γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ῥηθεῖσα ὑπὸ κυρίον: Ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ καὶ χρόνῳ προσφέρειν μοι θυσίαν καθαράν. ὅτι βασιλεὺς μέγας εἰμί, λέγει κύριος, καὶ τὸ ὄνομά μου θαυμαστὸν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι.
thought_title: The pure sacrifice on the Lord's day
orientation: The community is being instructed on how to gather for the Eucharist on the Lord's day, with reconciliation required before the sacrifice.
pass_a_gloss: On the Lord's day of the Lord, having gathered, break bread and give thanks, having confessed beforehand your transgressions, so that your sacrifice may be pure. But everyone who has the dispute with his companion must not come together with you, until they are reconciled, so that your sacrifice may not be defiled. For this is the one spoken by the Lord: In every place and time to offer me a pure sacrifice. Because a great king I am, says the Lord, and my name is wonderful among the nations.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'Lord's day' for κυριακή, not Sunday.
The verb form of εὐχαριστία; glossary bans 'thanksgiving' as noun rendering for the meal, but the verb is rendered literally as 'give thanks' to preserve the action.
Literal sense of a matter between two parties; 'dispute' captures the interpersonal conflict context.
The passive of κοινόω means to be made common/unclean; 'defiled' fits the sacrificial purity context.
Literal rendering of the plural dative; preserves the biblical phrase.

bible_refs.note: Ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ καὶ χρόνῳ προσφέρειν μοι θυσίαν καθαράν
ὅτι βασιλεὺς μέγας εἰμί, λέγει κύριος, καὶ τὸ ὄνομά μου θαυμαστὸν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι

pass_b_english: On the Lord's day, gather together, break bread, and give thanks, after you have confessed your transgressions, so that your sacrifice may be pure.
Anyone who has a dispute with his companion must not join you until they are reconciled, so that your sacrifice may not be defiled.
For this is what the Lord has spoken: "In every place and time offer me a pure sacrifice, because I am a great king, says the Lord, and my name is great among the nations" (Malachi 1:11, 1:14).
notes: The source text contains 'ὁ??ʼ' after ἕως, indicating damage or uncertainty in the manuscript; the gloss renders the clause as 'until they are reconciled' based on the clear verb διαλλαγῶσιν.

last_rejected.quote: For this is what the Lord has spoken
last_rejected.source_quote: αὕτη γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ῥηθεῖσα ὑπὸ κυρίον
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'spoken by the Lord' (passive), not 'the Lord has spoken' (active).
last_rejected.fix: For this is what was spoken by the Lord:
last_rejected.ruling: ῥηθεῖσα ὑπὸ κυρίον is a divine passive; 'the Lord has spoken' correctly conveys the same meaning.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ καὶ χρόνῳ προσφέρειν μοι θυσίαν καθαράν. ὅτι βασιλεὺς μέγας εἰμί, λέγει κύριος, καὶ τὸ ὄνομά μου θαυμαστὸν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσι
last_rejected.why: The citation combines Malachi 1:11 and 1:14 but the Greek has 'offer' (infinitive) not 'bring'; 'wonderful' not 'great'; and adds 'in every...time' not in either verse.
last_rejected.ruling: Citation correctly identifies Malachi 1:11, 14; the Didache itself paraphrases the OT text, not the translator.

problems.why: These words are not found in Malachi 1:11‑14.

problems.quote: In the assembly confess your transgressions
problems.why: Same Greek word (ekklēsia) rendered differently; reader may think 'assembly' and 'church' are distinct institutions.

problems.quote: You, Almighty Master, created all things
problems.why: Same referent (God) given three different titles; reader may think 'Almighty Master' is a different divine figure.
problems.fix: Note that 'Almighty Master' is an epithet for God the Father.

problems.quote: In every place and time offer me a pure sacrifice, because I am a great king, says the Lord, and my name is great among the nations
problems.why: The quote blends Malachi 1:11 and 1:14 but the wording 'I am a great king' comes from 1:14 while 'my name is great among the nations' comes from 1:11; the citation conflates two separate verses with different contexts.
problems.fix: Note that the quote combines Malachi 1:11 and 1:14, not a single verse.
